Run a read-only MCP server giving remote access to a chTKCat instance

Source: R/mcp.R
chTKCat_mcp_http_server.Rd

Start a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server available through HTTP (Streamable HTTP transport) to give remote MCP clients (e.g., Claude Code) access to the MDBs of a chTKCat instance. The server provides the same read-only tools as chTKCat_mcp_server().

Usage

chTKCat_mcp_http_server(
  mcpHost = Sys.getenv("TKCAT_MCP_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
  mcpPort = as.integer(Sys.getenv("TKCAT_MCP_PORT", "8800")),
  mcpPath = "/mcp",
  host = Sys.getenv("TKCAT_HOST", "localhost"),
  port = as.integer(Sys.getenv("TKCAT_PORT", "9111")),
  https = as.logical(Sys.getenv("TKCAT_HTTPS", "FALSE")),
  anonymousUser = Sys.getenv("TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_USER", NA),
  anonymousPassword = Sys.getenv("TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_PASSWORD", ""),
  allowedOrigins = NULL,
  maxRows = 1000L,
  maxChars = 60000L,
  maxExecutionTime = 300L,
  maxBodySize = 2^20,
  cacheTime = 3600,
  ...
)

Arguments

mcpHost

the address on which the MCP server listens (default: TKCAT_MCP_HOST environment variable or "127.0.0.1"). Use "0.0.0.0" to listen on all the interfaces.

mcpPort

the port on which the MCP server listens (default: TKCAT_MCP_PORT environment variable or 8800)

mcpPath

the path of the MCP endpoint (default: "/mcp")

host

a character string specifying the host heberging the chTKCat database (default: TKCAT_HOST environment variable or "localhost")

port

an integer specifying the port on which the database is listening (default: TKCAT_PORT environment variable or 9111)

https

a logical indicating if the HTTPS protocol should be used to connect to the database (default: TKCAT_HTTPS environment variable or FALSE)

anonymousUser

the ClickHouse user to use for requests without Authorization header (default: TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_USER environment variable or NA ==> authentication is required). An empty string is equivalent to NA.

anonymousPassword

the password of anonymousUser (default: TKCAT_MCP_ANONYMOUS_PASSWORD environment variable or "")

allowedOrigins

requests with an Origin header are only accepted if this header is in this vector of origins (e.g., "https://tkcat.example.com"). Default: NULL ==> requests with an Origin header are rejected (MCP clients other than web browsers do not send this header).

maxRows

maximum number of rows returned by a query (default: 1000)

maxChars

maximum number of characters returned by a tool call (default: 60000). Longer outputs are truncated.

maxExecutionTime

maximum execution time of a query in seconds (default: 300)

maxBodySize

maximum size of a request body in bytes (default: 1048576)

cacheTime

number of seconds during which user connections and MDB data models are kept in memory (default: 3600)

...

additional parameters for chTKCat() (only the default driver, ClickHouseHTTP::ClickHouseHTTP(), is supported).

Value

No return value, called for side effects: the function runs the server until it is interrupted.

Details

The server is meant to be run as a service behind a reverse proxy (e.g., nginx) providing HTTPS: by default it only listens on the local interface (mcpHost = "127.0.0.1"). See vignette("TKCat-MCP", package = "TKCat") for deployment instructions.

Authentication. Clients authenticate with their chTKCat (ClickHouse) credentials provided in an HTTP Basic Authorization header (Authorization: Basic <base64 of "user:password">). Credentials are checked by ClickHouse and each client gets access to the MDBs readable by its own user. No credential is stored by the server, except in memory to keep the connections open (during cacheTime seconds). If anonymousUser is set (e.g., "default"), requests without Authorization header are processed with this user and anonymousPassword. Credentials are sent in clear text if HTTPS is not used.

Read-only access. As for chTKCat_mcp_server(), ClickHouse sessions are opened with the readonly = 2 setting and SQL queries are checked before being sent.

Protocol. The server is stateless: it does not create MCP sessions and answers each POST request with a single JSON response. It does not provide server-sent event streams (GET requests are rejected with a 405 status). Several instances can thus be run behind a load balancer.

Logging. Tool calls are logged on the standard error output (time, client address, user and tool name).

See also

chTKCat_mcp_server(), chTKCat()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## From a terminal (normally run as a service)
# TKCAT_HOST=localhost TKCAT_PORT=9111 \
#   Rscript -e "TKCat::chTKCat_mcp_http_server(mcpPort = 8800)"
} # }
